characterList.description: A person wearing blue gloves and a blue long-sleeved gown, preparing and staining blood smears on slides.
characterList.name: Technician

content_metadata.description: An instructive and educational video on preparing and staining blood smears for microscopic examination.

qAndA.question: What type of tube should be used for preparing blood smears?
What is the ideal angle for holding the spreader slide?

qAndA.answer: Holding the spreader slide too high, resulting in wobbly and uneven smears.
qAndA.question: What is the 'shaky slide syndrome'?

qAndA.answer: Formalin fumes can damage the cells on the smears, rendering them useless for examination.
qAndA.question: Why is it not recommended to put smears in the same container as formalin-fixed tissues?

qAndA.answer: Five dips, one second per dip.
qAndA.question: How many dips are required for each staining solution?
